patch_description:
The failure was not caused by a bug in the ansatz specification or Python code. The stderr/stdout show `Evaluation error: [Errno 116] Stale file handle`, which is an OS/filesystem-level error occurring on the compute node (a1114u32n01) while the evaluation harness tried to read/write files (likely due to an NFS mount issue or a transient cluster filesystem glitch during job execution, not related to the ansatz content). Additionally the "conda: command not found" message indicates an environment activation issue in the shell init file, which is also outside the scope of the ANSATZ_SPEC file and unrelated to code correctness.

Since ANSATZ_SPEC itself is syntactically valid, uses only allowed gates (RY, RZ, CZ) with valid wire indices (0-7), valid parameter names, and a reasonable parameter count, there is no actual bug in the circuit specification to fix. The fix here is to ensure the program is self-contained, uses no external file I/O of its own, and resubmit unchanged so that the transient stale-file-handle condition (a filesystem caching issue on the cluster, unrelated to this file) does not recur. I verified the gate list, wire indices, and param strings are all valid per the schema, and kept the code structure identical to guarantee it still satisfies the fixed run_experiment interface.
